svg.title: Point detection after field extension
svg.desc: The generic prime of k[t] becomes the closed rational point t=a over k(a). Derived residue fields detect arbitrary unbounded complexes. A finite normal Koszul resolution computes point Hom. Global stack adjunction and spectral base change remain explicit hypotheses.

g.text: Residue fields and point delta tests
Full unbounded affine scope; precise global adjunction premises
1. A generic prime becomes a closed rational point [FE.7–FE.8]
Spec K[t], K = k(a)
Spec k[t]
closed point: (t − a)
generic point: (0)
projection
K[t] → K, t ↦ a; a is transcendental over k.
F = k(t): old closed fibres vanish; the new derived fibre is K.
R lies in the colimit-closed stable category of all κ(p). [FE.3–FE.6]
2. Finite normal Koszul complexes test any unbounded target
Δ = D / (D t₁ + ··· + D t_d)
Fibre resolution: normal degrees −d, …, 0
Point Hom: normal degrees 0, …, d
Wedge duality and shift −d identify vanishing. [FE.10–FE.11]
The target complex may have cohomology in every integer degree.
3. What the chart detector proves, and what the stack needs
Nonzero M → nonzero affine chart → field extension → point Hom ≠ 0
This detects the full operator-module category. [FE.12–FE.13]
To test a global projected object, supply actual adjunctions:
Hom(P L_T(K), F_K) ≃ Hom(L_T(K), U F_K) ≃ T(U F_K)
Orthogonality then gives zero; conservativity gives F = 0. [FE.14]
Global L_T and spectral base change remain explicit hypotheses.
